gold_output.simple_thesis: Buy MU as an AI memory-cycle upturn where HBM scarcity, data-center memory demand, and conservative earnings guidance can drive upside faster than the market is pricing.
gold_output.embedded_macro_exposure: Long AI infrastructure capex, memory pricing recovery, semiconductor cyclicals, and a lower-rate backdrop for capital-intensive growth.

mispricing.consensus_view: The market is likely still treating Micron as a cyclical memory stock whose earnings power can fade quickly after a rebound.
mispricing.variant_view: The AI data-center memory cycle is creating a structurally tighter HBM/DRAM environment, making this upcycle more durable and higher-margin than a normal memory rebound.
mispricing.pricing_evidence: The thesis cites MU at $131.37 against a $230-$300 target range based on normalized through-cycle EPS of $10-$12, implying 75-130% upside if the cycle thesis is right.
mispricing.why_consensus_is_wrong: Consensus is underweighting HBM scarcity, supply discipline in the three-player DRAM oligopoly, and management's conservative beat-and-raise setup into September 2025 earnings.

catalyst_or_reason_now.why_now: The position was initiated ahead of earnings because the thesis expected further upside from HBM/data-center strength, and price action had already confirmed improving market sponsorship.
source_evidence: investment_theses/MU.md key catalyst: beat-and-raise earnings cadence on September 23, 2025

invalidation.observable: The earnings catalyst fails to confirm HBM/data-center memory strength or the stock rejects good news.
invalidation.metric_or_event: September 23, 2025 earnings, forward revenue/EPS guidance, HBM supply commentary, gross margin direction, and post-earnings price reaction.
invalidation.threshold: Invalidate or force review if guidance fails to show continued sequential revenue/EPS growth, management backs away from supply-tightness/HBM strength, gross margin outlook deteriorates, or MU breaks back below the 100D/150D/200D SMA cluster after earnings on thesis-relevant news.
invalidation.timeframe: Earnings event and the following 1-2 trading weeks.
invalidation.implication: The AI memory upcycle may be already priced, less durable than expected, or too early for actionable capital.

evidence_for.claim: Micron had clear AI memory-cycle support.
evidence_for.support: The thesis says AI-driven data-center buildout was generating supply-constrained HBM and NAND demand, with management indicating supply growth would trail industry demand growth through at least calendar 2025.

evidence_for.claim: The memory industry structure supported better pricing discipline.
evidence_for.support: The thesis frames DRAM as a consolidated three-player oligopoly with Micron, SK Hynix, and Samsung, reducing the likelihood of a disorderly supply response versus a fragmented industry.

evidence_for.claim: Valuation upside was large enough to clear the actionability bar.
evidence_for.support: The thesis cites a $230-$300 target range from $131.37, implying 75-130% upside if normalized earnings power of $10-$12/share is realized.

evidence_for.claim: Price action confirmed the thesis before the catalyst.
evidence_for.support: On 2025-09-05, MU closed above all selected moving averages with positive 1-month, 3-month, and 12-month rate of change.

evidence_against.support: The thesis notes the prior FY22-FY23 downturn erased about 50% of TTM revenue, so a demand correction could compress margins quickly.

evidence_against.claim: AI capex digestion is the main left-tail risk.
evidence_against.support: Any hyperscaler capex pause would reduce HBM and data-center NAND demand faster than supply can adjust.

evidence_against.claim: The target valuation assumes elevated earnings and a healthy multiple.
evidence_against.support: The thesis target of $230-$300 assumes 23-25x on $10-$12 EPS; multiple compression or an earnings miss would materially reduce upside.
